name: migration compiles against production-shaped text[] orders and captured legacy financial RPC
each product alone uses the same order/receipt/financial pipeline
mixed order: all three products settle atomically, exact commission, repeat is a no-op
credit failure rolls back every access/sale/registration; retry completes once
direct client money/paid/access/foreign-price mutations cannot bypass server checkout
nominal capacity=0 never blocks sales; no reservation/refund tables or booking expiry exist
unpaid cancellation has no access/sales effects; verified payment still settles atomically
repeat checkout and lost intent reuse one order; changed payload with same key is rejected
parallel callbacks produce one receipt, three sales, one registration
mixed promo discounts only eligible lines, no stacking; deposit amount/remaining preserved
one-kopeck fixed discount across three products has exact line/order sums
course-scoped promo does not discount another product
100% promo completes on server without fabricated payment/audit; repeat is idempotent
failed/unverified payment cannot grant access or credit
free event/course: atomic idempotent registration, no payment order, library arrays preserved
explicit renewal uses DurationPrice and preserves remaining paid time
existing lifetime entitlement remains lifetime
stream before/during/after live uses backing access; expired access window rejects purchase
opt-in stream recording and chat access survive shared checkout
legacy unpaid course order remains compatible; historical paid order is not reprocessed
buy=false placeholder is not a discounted renewal or a purchased product
mixed products by three authors credit each author separately with unchanged commission
legacy untyped cart row is resolved and repriced from canonical product, not shop price
payment-link single-flight/reuse, actor binding and old payment-link resumption
actual PostgREST: owner cart, foreign-row isolation, protected writes/service RPCs/private schema
editing nominal capacity cannot invalidate checkout or block confirmed payment
verify SQL passes; non-destructive rollback blocks new orders but preserves pending fulfillment
temporary services stopped; loopback ports closed
